questions.q: What is the general ledger (GL)?
options: The company's main accounts, holding totals per account
A list of every customer's payments
questions.reason: The GL keeps totals; FSCD keeps the detail per customer.

questions.q: Why is FSCD called a sub-ledger?
options: It keeps the detail per customer and sends totals to the GL
questions.reason: Each night FSCD sums postings per GL account and transfers the totals.

questions.q: What is a reconciliation account?
options: The GL account whose balance must equal the total of FSCD open items
questions.reason: Account 140000 Receivables in our example: its balance equals all customers' open items in FSCD.

questions.q: What is the 'golden rule' of FSCD and the GL?
options: Total FSCD open items = balance of the reconciliation account
The GL always has more lines than FSCD
Every customer has their own GL account
questions.reason: Reconciliation proves this every month.

questions.q: What does account determination do?
options: Finds the GL accounts automatically from company code, product and main/sub transaction
questions.reason: Nobody types GL accounts; configuration tables map the type of money to accounts.

questions.q: When Mette's DKK 8,000 premium is billed, what are the debit and credit?
questions.reason: The customer now owes money (asset up) and the company earned premium income.

questions.q: Where does the DKK 88 insurance tax go on the credit side?
questions.reason: Tax collected from customers is owed to the tax authority, so it's a liability.

questions.q: When the direct debit is collected, what happens to Receivables?
questions.reason: Debit bank clearing, credit receivables: the customer no longer owes it.

questions.q: Which account receives the DKK 100 return fee on the credit side?
questions.reason: A separate main/sub transaction for fees maps to a fee income account.

questions.q: After all of Mette's postings, what is her total on account 140000?
When the DKK 25,000 claim is approved, what is debited?
questions.reason: Debit claims expense, credit payables to policyholders. The payment run later clears the payable.

questions.q: A new fee type is requested. What must exist before it can post correctly?
options: A main/sub transaction with its account determination
questions.reason: Without account determination the posting fails or lands on the wrong account.

questions.q: What is the life cycle of a reconciliation key?
options: Open, collect postings, close, transfer, reconcile
questions.reason: Only closed keys are transferred to the GL.

questions.q: Which job transfers FSCD totals to the general ledger?
questions.reason: The GL transfer takes closed, not-yet-transferred reconciliation keys and posts totals per account.

questions.q: Why might a reconciliation key fail to transfer?
options: A missing GL account or a closed GL posting period
The bank is closed on Sundays
questions.reason: The key stays 'not transferred' until the cause is fixed and the job runs again.

questions.q: FSCD open items and the GL differ at month-end. What is a common cause?
options: A reconciliation key still open or not transferred
questions.reason: Close the key and run the GL transfer; the difference disappears.

questions.q: Why should reconciliation accounts be blocked for manual GL postings?
options: Manual postings there break the match with FSCD
questions.reason: Only FSCD should post to them, through the GL transfer.

questions.q: What is FPO1 used for in reconciliation?
options: Listing FSCD open items at a key date
questions.reason: Its total is compared with the reconciliation account balance on the same date.

questions.q: What is foreign currency valuation at month-end?
options: Revaluing open items in a foreign currency at the month-end rate
questions.reason: For example SEK items in a Danish company are revalued so their DKK value is current.

questions.q: What is a receivables ageing report?
options: Open items grouped by how overdue they are (0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ days)
The age of the SAP system
questions.reason: Finance uses it to estimate bad debt and set a provision.

questions.q: What is the difference between written and earned premium?
options: Written = billed; earned = the part of the period already insured
Written premium is only for life insurance
questions.reason: FSCD posts written premium; earned premium and the unearned reserve are usually calculated in finance or actuarial systems.

questions.q: What's a good first step for a BA to learn their project's finance integration?
options: Walk through last month's reconciliation with finance
questions.reason: Seeing which keys, accounts and differences finance checks teaches the real process fastest.
